author: goldturtle
body:
@marcfeuermann @pgaudet: submitted with the PAINT issue template's fields. The posting account cannot set labels, so please add `PAINT annotation`.

* **PTHR ID & PTN node:** PTHR22800; PTN002503915 (gain of stimulatory C-type lectin receptor signaling pathway, GO:0002223); PTN002503915 (gain of positive regulation of natural killer cell mediated cytotoxicity, GO:0045954)

* **Sequences with problematic annotation (ID + gene/protein name):** UniProtKB:P26715 KLRC1 (killer cell lectin like receptor C1)

* **Type of Issue:** Erroneous propagation: activating-receptor terms reach the inhibitory receptor KLRC1 from its paralogs.

*How this draft was made:* an automated screen compared every PAN-GO (IBA) annotation of human genes (release 2025-10-12_2.0.5, PANTHER 19) with the genes' experimental annotations in GO release 2025-10-10. Flagged annotations were then judged by evidence-cited reasoning (Claude subagents, citing only a curated evidence pack). The statements below were checked against the GO, PAN-GO and PANTHER data, and the papers behind the key annotations were read. Please treat it as a candidate for curator review.


*The first term conflicts only indirectly: GO says that stimulatory C-type lectin receptor signaling positively regulates immune response and innate immune response, which KLRC1's negative-regulation annotations reach only through those ancestors. The second term conflicts directly. KLRC1 already inherits the opposite terms (negative regulation of natural killer cell mediated cytotoxicity and of T cell mediated cytotoxicity) from PTN002736229, the node where a loss is proposed, with KLRC1 itself as evidence. Two of the three evidence genes are partner chains: KLRD1 (CD94) pairs with the inhibitory NKG2A as well as the activating NKG2C and has negative-regulation IDAs from the same two papers as KLRC1 ([PMID:9485206](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/9485206/), [PMID:9486650](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/9486650/)). KLRE1 forms an inhibitory or an activating receptor depending on its partner (shown for rat KLRE1, [PMID:18713988](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18713988/)), although the mouse Klre1 source paper ([PMID:14707119](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/14707119/)) reports it as activating.*

**Inherited:** KLRC1 `involved_in` *stimulatory C-type lectin receptor signaling pathway* ([GO:0002223](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO:0002223))

- **Gain:** PTN002503915 (speciation, Mammalia; human genes below: KLRC1, KLRC2, KLRC3, KLRC4, KLRD1), dated 2021-08-19.
- **Evidence genes (3):** Klre1 (MOUSE), KLRC2 (HUMAN), KLRD1 (HUMAN).
- **Relation to KLRC1:** paralogs: Klre1 (MOUSE), KLRC2 (HUMAN), KLRD1 (HUMAN).
- **Other human genes inheriting it:** KLRC2, KLRC3, KLRC4, KLRD1.
- **Losses of this term in the family:** none.
- **v1 (paper release):** not annotated.

**Inherited:** KLRC1 `involved_in` *positive regulation of natural killer cell mediated cytotoxicity* ([GO:0045954](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO:0045954))

- **Gain:** PTN002503915 (speciation, Mammalia; human genes below: KLRC1, KLRC2, KLRC3, KLRC4, KLRD1), dated 2021-08-19.
- **Evidence genes (3):** Klre1 (MOUSE), KLRC2 (HUMAN), KLRD1 (HUMAN).
- **Relation to KLRC1:** paralogs: Klre1 (MOUSE), KLRC2 (HUMAN), KLRD1 (HUMAN).
- **Other human genes inheriting it:** KLRC2, KLRC3, KLRC4, KLRD1.
- **Losses of this term in the family:** none.
- **v1 (paper release):** not annotated.

**KLRC1's own experimental annotations** (GO release 2025-10-10) against *stimulatory C-type lectin receptor signaling pathway*: 3 opposing, 0 supporting:

- *negative regulation of T cell mediated cytotoxicity* ([GO:0001915](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO:0001915)): [PMID:9485206](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/9485206/) (IDA)
- *negative regulation of natural killer cell mediated cytotoxicity* ([GO:0045953](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO:0045953)): [PMID:9485206](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/9485206/) (IDA), [PMID:9486650](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/9486650/) (IDA)

**KLRC1's own experimental annotations** (GO release 2025-10-10) against *positive regulation of natural killer cell mediated cytotoxicity*: 2 opposing, 0 supporting:

- *negative regulation of natural killer cell mediated cytotoxicity* ([GO:0045953](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO:0045953)): [PMID:9485206](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/9485206/) (IDA), [PMID:9486650](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/9486650/) (IDA)

**Literature (Textpresso, all species corpora):** 8 sentences mention KLRC1 together with *immune response*. By cue words, 3 describe the opposite of the inherited direction and 1 agree.

> In the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME), inhibitory interactions between cancer and immune cells impair antitumoral immunity. **KLRC1 gene encodes the NK cell inhibitory receptor NKG2A, which is a potent NK cell immune checkpoint.** NKG2A specifically binds HLA-E, a non-classical HLA class I molecule frequently overexpressed in tumors, leading to the transmission of inhibitory signals that strongly impair NK cell function.

— Mac Donald A, Guipouy D, Lemieux W, Harvey M, Bordeleau LJ, Guay D et al. (2023). KLRC1 knockout overcomes HLA-E-mediated inhibition and improves NK cell antitumor activity against solid tumors. *Frontiers in immunology*. [PMID:37675109](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37675109/).


> CD274, CD86 and LGALS3 were more robustly expressed in relevant myeloid cell populations when compared to PDCD1LG2, CD80, CLEC4G and FGL1, which were either absent or minimally expressed in our dataset (Extended Data Fig. 4h). **Top predicted co-inhibitory interactions between human plaque immune cells included HLA-E and KLRC1 (encoding NKG2A), HMGB1 and HAVCR2 (encoding TIM3), and CD47 and SIRPA (encoding SIRPα) (Extended Data Fig. 4a).** The HLA-E–KLRC1 axis, a promising cancer IC target36, was predicted to signal most strongly between T and NK cells (Extended Data Fig. 5a).

— Barcia Durán JG, Das D, Gildea M, Amadori L, Gourvest M, Kaur R et al. (2024). Immune checkpoint landscape of human atherosclerosis and influence of cardiometabolic factors. *Nature cardiovascular research*. [PMID:39613875](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39613875/).


**Sentences counted as agreeing** (1): it describes editing out KLRC1 to restore NK-cell cytotoxicity. That fits KLRC1 as an inhibitory receptor, so it agrees with KLRC1's own annotations, not with the inherited term.

> NKG2A specifically binds HLA-E, a non-classical HLA class I molecule frequently overexpressed in tumors, leading to the transmission of inhibitory signals that strongly impair NK cell function. **Methods: To restore NK cell cytotoxicity against HLA-E+ tumors, we have targeted the NKG2A/HLA-E immune checkpoint by using a CRISPR-mediated KLRC1 gene editing.** Results: KLRC1 knockout resulted in a reduction of 81% of NKG2A+ cell frequency in ex vivo expanded human NK cells post-cell sorting.

— Mac Donald A, Guipouy D, Lemieux W, Harvey M, Bordeleau LJ, Guay D et al. (2023). KLRC1 knockout overcomes HLA-E-mediated inhibition and improves NK cell antitumor activity against solid tumors. *Frontiers in immunology*. [PMID:37675109](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37675109/).


**Reasoning on *stimulatory C-type lectin receptor signaling pathway*** (evidence-cited; verdict *error likely*, high confidence; cause: paralog inheritance): KLRC1 (NKG2A) is consistently described in the pack as an inhibitory NK cell receptor and immune checkpoint, and its own IDA annotations from two papers place it in negative regulation of NK and T cell cytotoxicity. The inherited 'stimulatory C-type lectin receptor signaling' term comes only from paralogs such as the activating receptor KLRC2, across a duplication node. The annotation is new in this release and should be removed from KLRC1.

- *Against:* KLRC1 has IDA annotations from two independent papers to negative regulation of natural killer cell mediated cytotoxicity, plus negative regulation of T cell mediated cytotoxicity. ([PMID:9485206](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/9485206/); [PMID:9486650](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/9486650/))
- *Against:* Sentences and abstracts call KLRC1/NKG2A an NK cell inhibitory receptor and immune checkpoint, and disrupting KLRC1 restores or improves NK cell killing of HLA-E+ targets. (Zhao et al. 2022; Mac Donald et al. 2023; Bexte et al. 2024)
- *Against:* The evidence genes are all paralogs (Klre1, KLRC2, KLRD1), and KLRC1 meets them at a duplication node; the paralog KLRC2 is modelled with activating MHC class Ib receptor activity, a role opposite to KLRC1's. (Klre1; KLRC2; KLRD1; PANTHER tree; gomodel:67369e7600000015)
- *Against:* The term is defined as signaling that results in cellular activation, which does not fit an inhibitory receptor. (GO definition)
- *Context:* The annotation was absent in PAN-GO v1; it was introduced by a gain curated in 2021 at a Mammalia node. (PAN-GO v1; PAN-GO annotation)

*Reasoner's suggested fix:* Add a loss of stimulatory C-type lectin receptor signaling pathway at PTN002736229 (KLRC1 subclade).

**Reasoning on *positive regulation of natural killer cell mediated cytotoxicity*** (verdict *error likely*, high confidence; cause: paralog inheritance): KLRC1 (NKG2A) inherits 'positive regulation of NK cell mediated cytotoxicity' only from paralogs such as the activating receptor KLRC2, but two independent IDA papers and three knockout studies show KLRC1 is an inhibitory receptor whose loss increases NK killing. The positive annotation spread from activating paralogs across a duplication and should not apply to KLRC1.

**Suggested change:**

- Add a loss (NOT) of *stimulatory C-type lectin receptor signaling pathway* at **PTN002736229** (speciation, Catarrhini; human genes below: KLRC1). KLRC1's lineage meets the evidence genes only at gene duplications (KLRC2 (HUMAN) at PTN002736221; Klre1 (MOUSE), KLRD1 (HUMAN) at PTN008582134), so the function may have diverged after duplication.
- Add a loss (NOT) of *positive regulation of natural killer cell mediated cytotoxicity* at **PTN002736229** (speciation, Catarrhini; human genes below: KLRC1). KLRC1's lineage meets the evidence genes only at gene duplications (KLRC2 (HUMAN) at PTN002736221; Klre1 (MOUSE), KLRD1 (HUMAN) at PTN008582134), so the function may have diverged after duplication.

### References
- Barcia Durán JG, Das D, Gildea M, Amadori L, Gourvest M, Kaur R et al. (2024). Immune checkpoint landscape of human atherosclerosis and influence of cardiometabolic factors. *Nature cardiovascular research*. [PMID:39613875](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39613875/).
- Bexte T, Albinger N, Al Ajami A, Wendel P, Buchinger L, Gessner A et al. (2024). CRISPR/Cas9 editing of NKG2A improves the efficacy of primary CD33-directed chimeric antigen receptor natural killer cells. *Nat Commun*. [PMID:39349459](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39349459/).
- Mac Donald A, Guipouy D, Lemieux W, Harvey M, Bordeleau LJ, Guay D et al. (2023). KLRC1 knockout overcomes HLA-E-mediated inhibition and improves NK cell antitumor activity against solid tumors. *Frontiers in immunology*. [PMID:37675109](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37675109/).
- Zhao XF, Huffman LD, Hafner H, Athaiya M, Finneran MC, Kalinski AL et al. (2022). The injured sciatic nerve atlas (iSNAT), insights into the cellular and molecular basis of neural tissue degeneration and regeneration. *eLife*. [PMID:36515985](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36515985/).
title: PAINT issue: PTHR22800: KLRC1 inherits "stimulatory C-type lectin receptor signaling pathway" and "positive regulation of natural killer cell mediated cytotoxicity", contrary to its own experimental annotations
